transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-22
- Start: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~68 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood Product), Alex (SilverStream HoS), Tara (Eng Mgr), Diego (CTO), Mina (Data Sci)

Summary:
Quick hosted-API demo focused on embeddings + reranking flow for SilverStream's site search. Walked through Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint, vector store integration pattern, and the two-step retrieval + rerank pipeline using Redwood rerank endpoint. Discussed perf tradeoffs (batching, caching, model choice), security (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for a 2-week pilot with a 100k-doc corpus.

Topics covered:
- Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint + common vector-store patterns
- Rerank endpoint: API shape, inputs (candidate ids + query + context), outputs (score + re-ranked text)
- Console demo: request logs, token cost heatmap, per-route latency breakdown
- Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching recommendations and quantization guidance
- Pilot scope, success criteria, security checklist

Transcript (timestamped, imperfect transcription typical of voice-to-text):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll get started. I'm Jordan from Redwood, that's Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus on product. How're you all doing?
[00:07] Alex: Good, yeah thanks. We've been looking forward to this, we're trying to reduce bad search results and cut down on time to relevant content.
[00:12] Tara: Morning from our side, a quick heads up we're on a tight Q2 timeline so want to understand how fast we can pilot.
[00:18] Jordan: Totally, that's the goal today — show a quick path to a hosted pilot. We'll do a short overview then Priya will jump into the console and code.
[00:26] Priya: Cool, I'll share my screen. So here's the embeddings endpoint, typical POST /v1/embeddings, you send text, get back a vector. For our hosted flow customers usually put these into a vector DB like Pinecone or an open-source store. With Redwood we also recommend prefix caching for repeated docs to save tokens.
[00:43] Mina: Quick Q — do you recommend batching client-side or let Redwood handle batching?
[00:47] Priya: Great question. For hosted API we do automatic batching in the runtime, but client-side micro-batches (100-200 docs) help with throughput during ingestion. The Optimize module will suggest batch sizes based on your seq lengths.
[00:58] [00:58] Jordan: also note, if you have long documents we recommend chunking with semantic overlap, keeps embeddings stable.
[01:06] Tara: What's the expected cost ballpark for 100k docs?
[01:09] Jordan: It depends on model and vector dim, but I can share an example calc — for a mid-tier embedding model it's roughly X tokens per doc during embedding, on the order of a few hundred dollars for one-time ingestion for 100k. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[01:22] Priya: Switching to retrieval + rerank — canonical pattern: retrieve top-N with ANN, then call Redwood reranker to rescore top 20. This gets you much better precision for short queries.
[01:32] Alex: How does the reranker API look?
[01:34] Priya: It's a JSON payload: query, candidates array (id, text, optional metadata), and you can pass metadata filters; response returns scores, optionally highlights, and the top-k ordering. We also support streaming partial scores if you want progressive UX.
[01:47] [01:47] Marcus: Live demo time — here's the console request inspector, you can see per-route metrics, per-token cost breakdowns. Notice the token heatmap for the rerank calls when we switched from a 512 to 256 context — latency dropped ~18% in this test.
[02:06] Diego: What about model variants — like can we fallback to quantized models if needed?
[02:10] Priya: Yes, Redwood has model variants tuned for cost — quantized 8-bit variants are available for some open models. You can set routing policies: prefer low-latency, or prefer low-cost, or set hard fallbacks to a cheaper model when dedicated capacity is congested.
[02:25] Mina: Is the reranker running on the same infra as embeddings? Any data residency concerns?
[02:29] Jordan: For hosted it's in our control plane and compute. We support private deployments and VPC connectors for customers that require that. For hosted we can also scope data retention and bring-your-own KMS for encryption at rest.
[02:43] Alex: We need SOC2 and audit logs — do you expose per-request logs for compliance?
[02:48] Priya: Yes, Console has request logs, and for enterprise customers we push detailed audit logs to customer S3 or syslog; SOC 2 is supported and we have ISO roadmap items.
[02:59] [02:59] Jordan: Quick live test — I'm going to run a sample query against SilverStream's demo corpus. Priya, do you want to narrate?
[03:05] Priya: Sure, running a retrieval for "how to claim royalty correction" — retrieval returns 100 candidates, we pass top 20 to rerank. Notice the rerank bumps the legal FAQ above a generic blog post.
[03:18] Alex: That looks promising, especially for ambiguous queries. Does the reranker expose explainability or why it scored something higher?
[03:24] Priya: We return per-candidate score and optional token-level highlights. For deeper explainability we pipe those into an eval set to show feature changes across rollouts. Optimize also tracks metrics tied to a query set.
[03:36] Tara: Can the reranker incorporate business signals like recency or click-through?
[03:40] Priya: Yes, you can attach metadata scores (recency, click-prior) and either include them as features for the reranker or post-merge with the rerank score. We showed a combined-score approach in the deck.
[03:51] [03:51] Marcus: Note on latency — rerank is O(N*K) on the model scoring side but we keep K small (20) and apply small models for scoring to meet p95 SLOs. For tail latency we use continuous batching and KV cache touches to reduce repeated work.
[04:07] Mina: Any gotchas with embeddings dimension mismatch across providers?
[04:11] Priya: Keep dims consistent; if you change models mid-pipeline we recommend a compatibility layer or reindexing. Redwood's Optimize warns when model change will break nearest-neighbor index.
[04:24] Alex: Security question — key rotation and SSO?
[04:28] Jordan: We integrate with SAML/Okta for SSO, support RBAC in Console, and have KMS integrations for key rotation. For pilot we can enable short-lived creds and keep audit trails.
[04:40] [04:40] Priya: Switching to sample code: here's the node/python snippet calling embeddings, then the rerank endpoint. Note we add candidate metadata with scores from your click model. I'll paste this into the shared slack channel after the call.
[04:56] Tara: Could you run a quick perf test with our index?
[04:59] Priya: Yes, if you share a sample index we can run a benchmark. It usually takes a few hours to run the end-to-end rerank bench for 100k, but we can do a targeted 10k run in a couple hours.
[05:12] [05:12] Jordan: For success criteria you mentioned improving click-through or mean reciprocal rank — what metric do you want to focus on?
[05:18] Alex: MRR and time-to-first-click are priority, also reduce zero-result queries.
[05:24] Mina: We'll provide a 500 query seed set and click labels.
[05:27] [05:27] Priya: Great. I'm going to toggle Optimize suggestions — here's a recommended batch size and a quantization profile. Optimize suggests a 32ms batch interval for your query volume and a 16-bit quant profile for the mid model population.
[05:43] Diego: Any SLA we can expect on hosted?
[05:46] Jordan: Hosted has commercial SLAs for Enterprise customers; for pilots we provide best-effort and can move to dedicated pools if you need strict SLOs. Dedicated pools give you predictable throughput and isolation.
[05:57] [05:57] Alex: Cost modeling — are there tools we can use to estimate monthly spend at 5M queries?
[06:02] Marcus: Yes, we have a cost estimator sheet we will share. It factors in token counts, rerank calls per query, and expected cache hit rates. We'll run numbers for your current traffic profile.
[06:15] Priya: Quick demo of Console: here's request logs, trace links into your application, and token-level cost breakdown. You can set per-route quotas to protect budget.
[06:27] Tara: About private deploy — if we need to host on AWS in our VPC, how much lead time?
[06:31] Priya: For VPC/connectors it's a couple of days for onboarding; for full on-prem/private install it's longer, typically weeks and depends on procurement windows. Pilot via hosted with VPC peering is usually fastest.
[06:45] [06:45] Jordan: We're nearing the end, last questions?
[06:48] Alex: How do rollouts work if reranker weights change? We need safe canaries.
[06:53] Marcus: Console supports canaries and A/B rollouts with automatic rollback based on eval-set regressions. You can pin old model and route a small percentage.
[07:03] Mina: Any limitations with very short queries? We see many 1-3 word queries.
[07:07] Priya: Short queries benefit a lot from rerank after retrieval. We often expand queries or use synthetic context to improve signals.
[07:18] [07:18] Jordan: Alright, recap of next steps: we'll share the quickstart repo, run a benchmark on a sample index, send pricing, and align on pilot dates.
[07:28] Alex: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:31] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the links and action items.

Notes on transcript quality / oddities: occasional mis-hear of "KV cache" as "K V cash", some proper nouns like model names were abbreviated in speech and transcription sometimes wrote "red wood". There was a bit of crosstalk when Alex interrupted during the live demo.
